images.caption:
20-0081-1342
electronic
First and Finest - Heroes Work Here. COVID-19 Response.  Cmdr. Tyler Warkentien, Naval Medical Center Portsmouth’s (NMCP) Public Health Emergency Officer and Infectious Disease Physician, is helping to lead the fight against COVID-19. He has helped to advance the planning, preparation, and collaboration of the hospital’s leadership, as well as communicating with staff to keep them safe, informed, and #ReadyForTheFight.
Warkentien hopes that the impact of his work at NMCP is allowing staff and patients to have more peace of mind and to gain access to the information they need.
“COVID-19 affects all of us… but we’re all in this together,” said Warkentien. “If we keep up what we’re doing with social distancing, wearing facemasks, washing our hands and looking out for each other, it will continue to help us as we move forward through this pandemic.”
The great efforts put forth by Cmdr. Warkentien and the many others proves that #HeroesWorkHere at #NMCPFirstandFinest.

WeAreTheFightingSpirit #StopTheSpread #FlattenTheCurve #NavyMedicine
Photo by MCSN Ariana R. Torman

images.filename: First and Finest - Heroes Work Here. COVID-19 Response. 20-0081-1343 (49942779276).jpg
images.caption:
20-0081-1343
electronic
First and Finest - Heroes Work Here. COVID-19 Response.  Cmdr. Justin Lafreniere, Naval Medical Center Portsmouth’s (NMCP) Internal Medicine Residency Training Program Director and General Internal Medicine Physician, is at the forefront of NMCP’s COVID-19 response. Lafreniere has put together a staffing plan to create surge teams to care for potential COVID patients, made up of physicians, orthopedists, neurosurgeons and neurologists, who wouldn’t normally see these patients. He has also created multiple command-wide briefs to enhance communication strategies at the medical center, keeping NMCP’s staff and patients informed.
“As this crisis has happened, I needed to step up into a new role,” Lafreniere said. “The only reason I have been able to do that is because I have other folks on my team to fill in and keep the Residency Training Program functioning while I am tasked with doing something else.”
Lafreniere highlighted the ability of the command to address COVID-19 while keeping the day-to-day afloat.
“I think the biggest thing we’ve been able to do is to show everyone that when we all get on the same sheet of music and are working towards a common goal, we can accomplish the impossible,” Lafreniere said. “While it’s been incredibly time-consuming, at the same time, it’s been energizing to see everyone rally around a common cause and reach a common goal.”
Lafreniere would like to personally acknowledge Lt. Dave Oliver, Lt. Varea Costello and Lt. Ashley Fang for their outstanding hard work and dedication during this time.
The great efforts put forth by Lafreniere and the many others proves that #HeroesWorkHere at #NMCPFirstandFinest.

WeAreTheFightingSpirit #StopTheSpread #FlattenTheCurve #NavyMedicine
Photo by MCSN Ariana R. Torman

images.caption: PORTSMOUTH, Va. (Oct. 19, 2020) – Naval Medical Center Portsmouth (NMCP) is collecting COVID Convalescent Plasma (CCP) in an effort to help patients who are sick with COVID-19 fight the virus. Robert (Bob) F. McDonnell, former Governor of Virginia visited NMCP to donate plasma, Oct. 19. “The military service has been a part of my family for 70 years,” McDonnell said. “I learned that the medical center has its own plasma program and there it became an opportunity to give.” Convalescent plasma is the liquid part of blood that is collected from patients who have recovered from an infection. The antibodies present in convalescent plasma are proteins that may help a person fight the coronavirus. “This opportunity is great and it is our duty; to help and give back to the young men and women who are doing so much to protect us,” McDonnell said. “Anything I can do to give back to those heroes, I’m going to do.”  (U.S. Navy photo by Seaman Imani Daniels/Released)
